Abstract describes task-based fMRI in human participants and reports neural activity to emotional stimuli (I1, I3, I4 appear met). It does not specify that participants performed an emotion regulation task (I2 not demonstrated). Inclusion is uncertain from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study of implicit emotion processing (gender discrimination) in healthy human participants that reports task-related activation (amygdala BOLD response and functional connectivity) to emotional facial expressions. Although not an explicit regulation task, the meta-analysis includes passive viewing of emotional stimuli, so inclusion criterion for emotion-regulation/viewing is satisfied.

Task-based fMRI with human participants (OD/BPD and healthy controls) performing an oddball task requiring attention amid negative emotional distractors (interpretable as cognitive control of emotion/affective regulation), and reporting task-related activation differences. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI study in humans performing an explicit emotion regulation task (maintain/enhance/suppress) with patient (mTBI) and control groups and reporting task-related brain activation, meeting I1,I2,I3,I4; no exclusions met.

E2 met: study is a mentalizing/Prisoner's Dilemma fMRI task without instruction to amplify or dampen participants' own emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (not an emotion-regulation task).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in 9–19-year-olds and task-related amygdala activation (I1, I3, I4 met). However, it does not describe an emotion regulation instruction or strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other regulation), so I2 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria (E1, E2) are met.

EXCLUDED: The task (Multi-Source Interference Task) is a cognitive interference/inhibition task, not an emotion-regulation or emotion-viewing task. Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met: I2 (no emotion-regulation instruction or emotional stimuli). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1/E2 not applicable).

Included for full-text review: abstract reports task-based fMRI in never-depressed adults with reported amygdala hyper-reactivity (task-related activation). However the abstract does not specify an emotion regulation task, so I2 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria met from abstract.

No evidence participants were instructed to regulate or modulate their emotions; task was color-naming (modified Stroop) of death-related/negative/neutral words. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion met: I1, I4. Inclusion not met: I2 (emotion regulation task not demonstrated).

This article is a review (Exclusion E1). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study with original data), I2 (does not report participants performing an emotion regulation task), I3 (does not report original participant groups), I4 (does not report task-related brain activation results).

Excluded because the abstract reports a task-based fMRI cue-exposure study with alcoholic and social drinker groups and task-related activations (meets I1, I3, I4) but does not describe any emotion-regulation instructions (reappraisal, distancing, regulation during anticipation/cue) and appears to be passive cue-reactivity; therefore I2 is not met. No exclusion criteria are met (none).

This is a resting-state fMRI study with no task-based emotion regulation; no task-related activation results are reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation).

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI, uses distraction as an emotion regulation strategy, involves human clinical and control groups, and reports task-related neural activation results. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to extract detailed ROI/contrast data.

Excluded: Study uses resting-state fMRI (no task); does not involve an emotion-regulation or viewing task and does not report task-related activation. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation).

Task-based fMRI study reporting anterior cingulate activation and amygdala connectivity during implicit emotion regulation in generalized anxiety disorder. Satisfies task-based imaging, emotion-regulation paradigm, and reports task-related activation. Unclear from abstract whether a separate control group is reported, so full-text review needed to confirm I3.

Abstract reports an emotional go/no-go task in adolescents addressing neural substrates of emotional reactivity and regulation, but it does not clearly state whether an explicit emotion-regulation instruction or fMRI activation results are reported. Inclusion is uncertain from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.
Study is resting-state FC, not a task-based emotion regulation fMRI study. No task or task-related activations are reported. Includes human clinical participants (I3) but does not meet I1, I2, or I4.

Excluded because the study does not meet I2: no emotion-regulation task was performed during fMRI (pressure-evoked pain used to assess CBT effects). Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Exclusion criteria met: none.

Study is an fMRI decision-making/ambiguity task, not an emotion regulation study. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). Inclusion not met: I2 (emotion regulation task not present). Exclusion criteria: none met (E1, E2 not applicable).

Resting-state fMRI study without any task or emotion-regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results).

No task-based fMRI or emotion-regulation task reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants with control groups). Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation). Study is structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry).

Task-based fMRI with human participants viewing emotional (angry) faces and reporting task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4 met). Abstract does not clearly indicate an instructed emotion-regulation task (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to determine whether regulation instructions or relevant contrasts are reported.

This is a resting-state rtfMRI neurofeedback training study, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation experiment. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). (c) Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I4 (no task-related brain activation reported), I2 (emotion-regulation during a task or regulation of responses to visual stimuli not demonstrated).

Task-based fMRI in humans reporting task-related activations (I1, I3, I4). Abstract does not clearly indicate an instructed emotion-regulation task or that participants performed regulation of visual stimuli (I2 not demonstrated); insufficient information to determine inclusion, so include for full-text review.

No emotion-regulation task is described (I2 not met): abstract reports passive exposure to cues without instructions to regulate. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human adolescent participants with control group), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1/E2 not applicable).

Study uses resting-state fMRI (no task), so it does not meet task-based fMRI inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants with control group), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (emotion regulation task) — the study used an emotional face-matching emotion-processing task without instructions to regulate responses.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (emotion regulation task) — the abstract reports THC effects on amygdala connectivity during viewing of social threat signals, with no instruction to regulate emotion. Therefore excluded.

Abstract/title do not specify whether this is a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study nor whether task-related brain activation results are reported. No exclusion criteria are evident. Insufficient information to determine inclusion from abstract alone — include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI with adolescents performing an emotional attention task, reporting task-related brain activation. It is unclear whether participants were instructed to regulate emotions (I2 ambiguous), but the study fits the review objective (viewing or regulating). Include for full-text review to confirm I2 eligibility.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants with control group), and I4 (task-related brain activation reported) are satisfied. I2 is not demonstrated: the study uses mindful introspection/self-reflection rather than instructions to regulate emotional responses to visual stimuli, so it does not meet the review objective.

The study does not manipulate or instruct emotion regulation (it used an emotional declarative memory/encoding task), so I2 (emotion regulation task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (clinical group with controls), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria apply (E1,E2 not met).

Exclusion: No emotion-regulation task. Exclusion criteria met: none (E1,E2 not applicable). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical patient with controls), I4 (reports task-related brain activations). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (not an emotion regulation task; study uses a motor go–nogo paradigm probing conversion paralysis and motor inhibition, not regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli).

Task-based fMRI with human clinical and healthy control groups reporting task-related brain activation. Include for full-text review to determine whether regulation instructions were used.

Abstract lacks sufficient information to determine whether this is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation or reports task-related activation. It appears empirical but does not describe tasks, participants, or results relevant to the review. Per guidelines, include for full-text review to assess I1–I4.

Abstract describes task-based fMRI in transgender persons examining neural response to ostracism (I1, I3, I4 met). It does not report an emotion regulation task or instructions to regulate emotional responses, and provides no evidence of reappraisal/other regulation or passive viewing of visual stimuli during regulation (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply.

Excluded (E2): study uses resting-state fMRI and social-cognition tasks (MASC, RMET) without emotion-regulation instructions. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical and control groups). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI; uses rs-fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation reported).

EXCLUDE: Study uses resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical participants with MDD). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation).

Study used a fear conditioning/extinction paradigm (passive learning of threat) rather than an instructed emotion-regulation task (e.g., reappraisal, acceptance, or other strategies). Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I2. No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

No emotion regulation task reported: I2 not met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). Exclusion criteria met: none. Task-based fMRI study of an emotional Stroop (implicit emotion regulation/adaptation) in healthy adolescent girls reporting task-related brain activation linked to model-based regulatory states. No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because participants did not perform an emotion regulation task (I2 not met): they viewed emotional faces and made perceptual judgments without instruction to regulate. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human children sample), I4 (reports task-related activation). No exclusion criteria met.

The abstract describes a structural neuroimaging study of resilience in police officers and does not report a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm or task-related activation results. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria explicitly met.

This study used a self-retrieval/self-reflection paradigm (self, ideal, avatar) rather than an instructed emotion-regulation task (e.g., reappraisal, distancing) for visual emotional stimuli. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion not met: I2 (no evidence of emotion-regulation instructions). No exclusion criteria clearly met (E2 not clearly applicable).

fMRI task with human participants and task-related activation reported, but abstract does not clearly state participants were instructed to regulate emotion (reappraisal) — it reports recruitment of reappraisal-related regions during anticipation. Abstract investigates emotional processing in adolescents with conduct disorder but does not clearly state whether a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm was used. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in PMDD (I1, I3). Excluded (E2): study uses self/other perspective and person-adjective matching without instructions to amplify or dampen participants' emotional responses, so it is not an emotion-regulation task (I2 not met). Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of emotional (fear) distractors during working memory in patients with schizophrenia, indicating task-related brain activation (I1, I4). Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in human clinical groups (OCD and SAD) using emotional visual stimuli, satisfying I1 and I3. No task-based fMRI or emotion-regulation task: study uses resting-state fMRI. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants with patient and control groups). Abstract reports fMRI connectivity during emotional reactivity in late-life GAD, indicating a task-based fMRI study with human clinical participants and task-related brain results. Abstract does not specify task-based fMRI, an emotion regulation task, or use of visual stimuli; it refers to olfactory emotion induction in schizophrenia (human participants). EXCLUDED. No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). fulltext_screening_results.reason: The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed cognitive reappraisal (Attend vs Reappraise) using visual stimuli (IAPS and alcohol images) in alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses with peak coordinates (MNI) and FWE-corrected inference, and the abstract and extracted data describe within-task effects (attend vs reappraise and emotional vs neutral) and group comparisons. All required elements for the meta-analysis are present: task fMRI, instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal), visual stimuli, eligible sample with control group, reported relevant task contrasts, and whole-brain coordinate results. No exclusion criteria from the list (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, or reporting only between-group contrasts with no task effects) are met based on the document. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the reported task used an auditory stimulus (participants attempted to lower the volume), so the study does not meet I7 (visual emotional stimuli). Also, instructions do not describe an instructed emotion-regulation strategy like reappraisal (I6 not met). Therefore the study fails key inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I9) and meets exclusion E6.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: I5 - it is a task-based fMRI study; I6 - it uses an instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) task with arrows to increase/decrease/maintain; I7 - stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (negative and neutral); I8 - samples (young and older healthy adults) are eligible; I9 - reports within-task regulation contrasts (downregulate > maintain; upregulate > maintain) and unregulated viewing contrasts (negative > neutral); I10 - reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space; I11 - results are reported in tables of peaks. No exclusion criteria apply (not non-empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group task effects, and not an empathy/perspective-taking only study). This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed a cognitive reappraisal emotion regulation strategy (I6) using visual IAPS pictures (I7). The study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs emotion regulation (diminish/enhance) (I6) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) (I7). The sample includes PTSD patients and non-PTSD controls with results reported (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain analyses are reported (not ROI-only), the results are task-evoked activation maps (not only connectivity), and within-group task effects are analyzed alongside between-group comparisons. Study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) where participants were instructed to use emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal up- and down-regulation) during the task (I6). The regulated stimuli were visual (pictures of male and female proposers) (I7). Sample is reported (n=21 healthy adults) (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly related to regulation (e.g. Up > Look and Down > Look contrasts) (I9). Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with FWE-corrected inference and peak coordinates in MNI space (I10), and these results are presented in tables (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, include within-group task effects, and the paradigm involves instructed emotion regulation rather than unconstrained perspective-taking. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were instructed to use emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (film clips and images). It includes within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > watch-negative; suppress > watch-negative) and an unregulated viewing contrast (watch-negative > watch-neutral). Analyses are group-level whole-brain voxelwise with reported peak coordinates in Talairach space and cluster-level inference (AFNI AlphaSim), with peaks listed in tables. Sample (n=17 healthy adults) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based whole-brain fMRI (I5, I10), an instructed cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task (explicit instruction to reappraise; I6), visual stimuli (IAPS pictures; I7), healthy adult sample (I8), and reports task-related contrasts (e.g. RU–CU, PU–CU; reappraise/placebo vs control) with peak coordinates in standard space (Talairach) (I9, I11). NeuroStore lists multiple whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and coordinate tables and the abstract describes reappraisal and placebo activation differences, indicating within-task regulation effects were reported. No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain results are present (so not E4/E5), and within-task contrasts are reported (so not E6). Full text appears available via the extracted NeuroStore record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (reappraisal/suppress blocks) (I6); uses visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) (I7); reports healthy adult participants (I8); includes within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Suppress > Maintain, Maintain > Suppress) (I9); and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results reported in MNI with peak coordinates (spatial scope whole brain, reported peaks) (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical (not E3), presents whole-brain analyses (not E4), is not limited to connectivity-only results (although it also reports ROI connectivity, whole-brain task maps are present, so not E5), reports within-group task effects (not E6), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking-only paradigm (not E7). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual IAPS images with a within-subject emotion regulation manipulation (Reappraise vs Baseline, and Maintain vs Baseline). It reports group-level voxelwise results in MNI space with reported peak coordinates. All required inclusion criteria are met: task-based fMRI (I5); instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal) during stimulus presentation (I6); visual stimuli (I7); eligible sample reported (healthy adults) (I8); within-task regulation contrast reported (Reappraise > Baseline) (I9); whole-brain spatial scope and reported coordinates (I10) and results reported as peaks/tables acceptable (I11). No exclusion criteria are met: although inference used small-volume correction within an ROI, the analysis is marked whole-brain and reports standard-space peaks, so E4 (ONLY ROI/SVC results) does not apply. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that manipulates an antecedent-focused reappraisal-like strategy by presenting precedent descriptions (extrinsic/incidental reappraisal) to modulate emotional responses (I6). Stimuli are visual photographs (IAPS and others) (I7). Participants are healthy adults (I8). The paper reports within-task emotion-related contrasts (unpleasant > neutral within contexts) satisfying the requirement for an emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrast (I9). Critically, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates are reported for real and fictitious contexts (whole-brain analyses with reported peaks), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements (I10) and acceptable reporting of coordinate tables/peaks (I11). No exclusion criteria are met. The reported ROI results (amygdala, insula) are accompanied by whole-brain maps, so E4 does not apply.

The study reports a task-based fMRI emotion regulation paradigm with visual IAPS stimuli and explicit reappraisal instructions (meets I5, I6, I7). It provides whole-brain, cluster-corrected peak coordinates (meets I10 and I11) and the sample (late-life depressed patients) is an eligible participant group (meets I8). However, all reported analyses are omnibus between-group contrasts (remission status × scan time) with no within-task/regulation contrasts reported (e.g., reappraise > look) or any within-group task effects. Therefore it violates exclusion E6 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria not met: I9. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal of anticipatory anxiety (I6). The sample (healthy adults, n=15) is acceptable (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., regulation > control, regulation > anxiety) (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met: results are whole-brain (not ROI-only), include within-group contrasts, and are not purely connectivity or non-empirical. The study is a task-based fMRI cognitive reappraisal study using visual IAPS stimuli in healthy participants, so it meets I5, I6, I7, and I8. However, the NeuroStore record shows only between-group interaction/group-comparison contrasts (HM > LM for down- and up-regulatory reappraisal) and does not report any within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look or down-regulate > maintain) or unregulated viewing contrasts for any group (failure to meet I9). Inference is reported as Small Volume Correction (pFWE) and the extracted analyses list SVC-only results/peaks, with no evidence of group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps or whole-brain inference (failure to meet I10). Therefore the study reports only between-group SVC results and no whole-brain or within-task effects, meeting exclusion criteria E6 and E4. Exclude on that basis.

Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli—IAPS images), I8 (sample includes patients and separately reported controls), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise results with peaks in MNI space), I11 (coordinates/tables clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (the study does not report any within-task contrast or unregulated viewing contrast for a single group; only between-group interaction contrasts are reported). This is a task-based fMRI study (n=76) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (detach/distancing vs permit), using visual stimuli (IAPS/EmoPicS). No exclusion criteria are met (not non-empirical, not connectivity-only, not ROI-only, not between-group-only, and the perspective-taking instruction is used specifically to reduce emotional involvement as a regulation strategy). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (I5,I6). Emotional stimuli are visual (faces; I7). Sample is healthy adults with group results reported (n=26; I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts such as reappraise > look (I9). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (reappraisal) and a maintain condition (I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). Participant groups include healthy controls and patient groups with results reported (I8). The report includes within-task contrasts relevant to regulation and unregulated viewing (Reappraise > Baseline; Maintain > Baseline) (I9). Although NeuroStore labels the contrasts as ‘omnibus, between-group’ in places, the presence of Reappraise>Baseline and Maintain>Baseline whole-brain contrasts with coordinates satisfies the meta-analysis requirements. The study is a task-based fMRI investigation that explicitly instructs emotion regulation via causal attributions (internal vs external), using visual stimuli (faces). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. internal>view, external>view, internal>external) for both healthy controls and MDD patients, and provides whole-brain, cluster-corrected voxelwise results with peak coordinates. Both participant groups are reported separately. No exclusion criteria apply (not only ROI/SVC, not only connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, not an empathy task without regulation). Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed cognitive reappraisal (participants instructed to detach/think as an objective third party) using visual IAPS images (positive, negative, neutral). It reports within-task contrasts directly related to regulation (Reappraise > Experience; Experience > Reappraise) and an age-group interaction contrast. Analyses are whole-brain, cluster-corrected with reported peak coordinates in MNI space. Although PPI connectivity analyses are reported, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps are also provided. The sample includes healthy younger and older adults. Therefore it meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

The study meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the review objective: it is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation task (cognitive reappraisal: 'Decrease Neg') with visual stimuli (neutral and negative pictures). Within-task regulation contrasts are reported (Decrease Neg > Look Neg and its reverse) for groups separately. At least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis is reported with standard-space coordinates and FWE correction (analyses report whole-brain FWE-corrected results and peaks in MNI space). A control group’s results are reported separately. Although some reported contrasts used small-volume correction, whole-brain results are present, so exclusion for ROI-only results does not apply. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore include.

The study reports task-based fMRI of instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal to increase/decrease responses to angry faces) with visual stimuli (faces), healthy sample, and within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Decrease > Observe; Increase > Observe) at the group level. Spatial scope is whole-brain with coordinates in MNI and reported peak tables. Although the paper also reports resting-state seed-based connectivity, it additionally provides whole-brain task-evoked maps, so exclusion E5 does not apply. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed cognitive reappraisal (reframe/ reinterpret to decrease negative emotion) using visual stimuli (72 static facial images from the NimStim set). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise-Negative > Maintain-Negative; Maintain-Negative > Look-Neutral) at the group level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI (tables of peaks reported), and uses an appropriate GLM/random-effects model. Participants are healthy adults (n=21). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and the task involves instructed emotion regulation rather than mere perspective-taking. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal to up- and down-regulate emotion (I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). Sample is a healthy adult group reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Increase > Look-Negative; Decrease > Look-Negative) (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates and tables are provided (Talairach space) and inference is whole-brain corrected (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes whole-brain activation maps and not only ROI or connectivity-only results. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study meets the meta-analysis requirements: it is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly investigates both emotion recognition and voluntary attentional regulation (the paper and record describe ‘voluntary attentional regulation’ and contrasts between emotion-evaluation and shape/orientation evaluation). Stimuli are visual IAPS pictures. First-level SRT versus ERT contrasts were modeled and used in second-level (group) comparisons (independent-samples t-test of SRT vs ERT contrasts), and whole-brain, cluster-level FWE-corrected results with peak coordinates in MNI space are reported. Therefore it provides within-task contrasts related to regulation/viewing and whole-brain peak coordinates suitable for meta-analysis.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment (BOLD) in which participants were instructed and trained to reduce negative emotion using cognitive reappraisal (Reduce vs Maintain). Stimuli were visual IAPS images. The paper reports a within-task regulation contrast (Reduce > Maintain) and whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (Talairach) and cluster-level correction. Participant groups (high-anxiety patients and healthy controls) are described and group-level results are reported separately. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and not an empathy task). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are met.

The NeuroStore record shows a task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive reappraisal (explicit downregulation) during presentation of visual IAPS images (emotion regulation task), with both Maintain and Reappraise conditions. The report includes within-task contrasts (Maintain > Reappraise and group interactions, pictures vs baseline) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with reported peak coordinates in MNI (tables of peaks referenced). A patient group (panic disorder) and healthy controls are reported separately. Although a seed PPI connectivity analysis is present, whole-brain activation maps are also reported (Table tbl2), so the study is not limited to ROI or connectivity-only results. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

The study meets several inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI; instructed emotion regulation using distraction and reappraisal; visual IAPS stimuli; healthy participant sample; and within-task contrasts such as reappraise > view and view negative > view neutral). However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest analyses with small-volume correction (ROI SVC) and no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps are reported. This violates inclusion criterion I10 and triggers exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI/SVC results reported). Therefore the study is excluded.

Excluded because the NeuroStore record indicates only region-of-interest (ROI) results and only between-group interaction contrasts were reported. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only ROI results reported; no whole-brain analysis) and E6 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported, with no within-group task effect reported). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—reappraisal and distraction), I7 (visual stimuli—IAPS images), I8 (sample includes clinical and control groups reported separately). (c) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I9 (no within-task/regulation contrast for any group reported in this document) and I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Based on the provided document, the study must be excluded because it violates E4 and E6. Full text appears complete in this record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (self-distraction) during an anticipatory anxiety paradigm, reports within-task regulation contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates. These meet inclusion criteria I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, and I11. However, the regulated stimuli are auditory cues (high/low pitch beeps) and painful electrical stimulation rather than visual stimuli; therefore inclusion criterion I7 (emotional stimuli are VISUAL) is NOT met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Because it fails I7, the study is excluded from this meta-analysis.

The paper reports a task-based fMRI study instructing cognitive reappraisal (regulate vs view) of visual IAPS images in healthy participants (n=14). It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (Reappraisal>View and View>Reappraisal) with FDR correction and reported peak coordinates in Talairach space, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task activation maps. The study also reports seed-based connectivity, but this is accompanied by the required whole-brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met. Note: the NeuroStore tag ‘between-group’ on the Reappraisal>View entry is likely a metadata label; the entry specifies a group GLM random-effects analysis of the task contrast and lists whole-brain corrected peaks, which fulfils the within-task contrast requirement.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment using visual stimuli (faces) with a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (faces > shapes) and reports whole-brain group-level results and coordinates; participants are healthy adults. However, the task did not instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy (instructions: match faces/shapes; explicitly 'no instructions to regulate emotion'). Although the paper reports correlations with trait ERQ reappraisal scores, this is observational (cross-subject regression) and not an instructed regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise > look). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) of emotional responses to visual stimuli (IAPS and spider pictures). Within-task contrasts related to regulation and unregulated viewing are reported (e.g. up/down vs look; spider vs aversive), and several analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps reported in MNI with peak coordinates and cluster inference. The sample is a clinical group (spider phobics) with within-group results presented. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group task effects are reported. Therefore it meets all relevant inclusion criteria and none of the exclusions.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli in an eligible sample (children and adults), the NeuroStore record reports only seed-based/effective connectivity analyses (Granger) and provides no clear within-task contrasts of instructed emotion regulation (e.g., reappraise > look, down-regulate > maintain) or an explicit whole-brain task-evoked activation map. The task appears to be an emotional Go/No-Go (response inhibition) paradigm rather than an instructed cognitive reappraisal or other explicit emotion-regulation instruction. Therefore the study does not meet the requirement for an instructed emotion-regulation task (I6) nor the requirement for a within-task regulation contrast (I9) or clearly reported whole-brain activation results (I10). Exclusion E5 applies because only connectivity results are reported without accompanying whole-brain task activation maps.

Excluded because the paper reports ONLY between-group interaction contrasts and does not present any within-group task activation maps. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli—IAPS images), I8 (sample includes patient and control groups reported), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported; MNI coordinates), I11 (results reported as peak coordinate tables). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no within-task contrasts for regulation or unregulated viewing reported in the document; NeuroStore extracts only between-group interaction contrasts). This study is a task-based fMRI experiment where participants were instructed to use cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) while viewing visual stimuli (photographs of proposers) during a Dictator Game. The NeuroStore record reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., up > look, down > look, up > down) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise inference and MNI peak coordinates. Participant sample is healthy and acceptable. All required inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI with instructed emotion regulation strategies (Detachment, Reinterpretation, Distraction, Expressive Suppression) using visual IAPS pictures; reports within-task contrasts (multiple ‘Regulate Negative > Permit Negative’ and Permit > Regulate contrasts) and valence contrasts; group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected peak coordinates in MNI space; sample reported (healthy participants, n=74, and subgroup within-group analyses). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group task effects).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI experiment with instructed emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) applied during stimulus presentation (I5,I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample is healthy adults and thus eligible (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation and viewing (e.g., reappraisal > view, distraction > view, view emotional > neutral) (I9). Results include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with peak coordinates in MNI space and tables of reported peaks (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is empirical (not E3), reports whole-brain activations (not only ROI or connectivity; so not E4/E5), includes within-group task effects (not only between-group; not E6), and involves instructed regulation rather than mere perspective-taking without regulation (not E7).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (distancing/perspective-taking reappraisal; I6), uses visual emotional stimuli (60 IAPS pictures; I7), includes an eligible sample of healthy participants (I8), reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g., regulation > no regulation, negative > neutral; I9), and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with peak coordinates in MNI space (several analyses report whole-brain FWE-corrected results and tables of peaks; I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are triggered: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), within-group task effects are present, and the task is explicit emotion regulation rather than mere perspective-taking without regulation. Thus the paper should be INCLUDED in the review.

Exclusion reasons: E4 (only region-of-interest / small-volume-corrected results reported; no whole-brain voxelwise analyses extracted) and E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effects reported). Excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: an emotion-regulation strategy was not instructed. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli — IAPS images), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports a within-task contrast related to emotion regulation: NNEG-DES > NEG-DES), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with peak coordinates in MNI), I11 (results reported as coordinate table). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E7 violations). Full text was available in the record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

All inclusion criteria are met: This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed an emotion-regulation strategy (reappraisal/distancing) during stimulus presentation (I6). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (WatchNeg > RegulateNeg and RegulateNeg > WatchNeg) (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are provided with peaks in MNI space and reported peaks (analysis_1 reports uncorrected whole-brain peak-level results; analysis_0 includes SVC but does not negate the presence of whole-brain results) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not exclusively ROI/SVC (E4), not only connectivity (E5), not only between-group contrasts (E6), and this is not a non-empirical paper (E3) nor an empathy task without regulation instruction (E7). All inclusion criteria are met: this is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (Increase/Decrease reappraisal trained), using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures and film clips), with healthy participants reported, and it reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Increase>Look, Decrease>Look). Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI and FWE-corrected inference. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group effects, and is not an empathy-only paradigm). The document appears to contain the necessary extracted results, so full text is not incomplete.

The study meets task-based fMRI criteria with instructed cognitive reappraisal of visual IAPS stimuli and reports within-task contrasts and control group (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied). However, all reported task-activation results are region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (Analyses 0 and 1: ROI, AlphaSim-corrected within ROI), and the only whole-brain result is a seed-based PPI connectivity analysis (Analysis 2). No group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates is reported, so inclusion criterion I10 is not met. This violates exclusion criterion E4 (ROI-only results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Therefore the study is excluded.

The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) voxelwise results (FWE within each ROI) with no whole-brain task-activation analysis, and it presents only between-group interaction contrasts and PPI connectivity results without any reported within-group task activation contrasts (reappraise > view) for any group. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain analysis) and E6 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported, no within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation; reappraisal and distraction), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS images), I8 (sample includes patients and matched controls reported separately). This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation in children/adolescents. The task explicitly instructs regulation (Look, More gross, Less gross; up- and down-regulation using a pretense strategy), uses visual stimuli (IAPS and child-appropriate images), and reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., decrease > look, increase > look, look > decrease). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported in Talairach space with peak coordinates and cluster-corrected inference (Monte-Carlo cluster correction), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Sample (n=15, ages 7–17) is acceptable per criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, not an empathy task without regulation). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs emotion regulation (Reappraise/Reframe vs React/Just Watch) (I6); the regulated stimuli are visual (color photographs of faces and videotaped social clips; film/video qualify) (I7); participant groups include patients and healthy controls with separate group results reported (I8); analyses include within-task regulation contrasts (Reappraise > React) (I9); results are whole-brain, voxelwise maps with peak coordinates in Talairach space (I10) and reported in tables (I11). Multiple within-group and between-group whole-brain contrasts are provided, so no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the paper is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual-stimulus emotion regulation fMRI studies.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment with an instructed mindfulness (acceptance-like) regulation strategy, visual IAPS stimuli, and a healthy sample, so it meets I5, I6, I7 and I8. However, the NeuroStore record shows only region-of-interest, region-level results (DMPFC peak) and reports a between-group interaction contrast; no within-task (e.g. regulate>view) contrasts or any whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps/peak coordinates are reported. Therefore it fails I9 and I10 and meets exclusion criteria E4 (ONLY ROI results reported) and E6 (ONLY between-group contrasts reported with no within-group task effect). Full text is available in the record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (spatial scope: region of interest; inference corrected within ROIs) with no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps. This violates inclusion criterion I10 and meets exclusion criterion E4. The paper otherwise meets the review topic and several inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal) (I6), uses visual stimuli (I7), includes an eligible sample with separate control group results (I8), and reports within-task contrasts/condition effects related to regulation (I9). However, because no whole-brain results are reported, it must be excluded (E4).

The NeuroStore record reports only between-group contrasts (analysis_0: marijuana users > controls during reappraisal; analysis_1: connectivity controls > users). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—distancing/reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli—IAPS), I8 (sample includes patients and controls reported separately), I10 (whole-brain group-level map reported with peaks in MNI), I11 (coords/peaks reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I9 (no within-task or unregulated viewing contrast reported). This triggers exclusion criterion E6 (studies reporting ONLY between-group contrasts with no within-group task effect). fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study investigates instructed cognitive reappraisal with visual stimuli in an fMRI task and reports whole-brain voxelwise results; however, the NeuroStore extraction lists only between-group interaction contrasts (patient vs control) and an age regression in controls, with no within-group task contrasts (e.g. reappraise > look) or unregulated viewing contrasts reported for either group. This means the paper reports only between-group contrasts/interactions and no within-group task effect, invoking exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation - cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample with reported control group), I10 (whole-brain group-level maps with coordinates), I11 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I9 (no within-task contrast or unregulated viewing contrast reported). Full text appears complete as represented by the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) using visual stimuli (IAPS and matched pictures) in healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g. reappraise > look, distract > look, reappraise > distract) and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with corrected whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates (Tables t1–t3) in MNI space. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text is available in the supplied record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Exclusion E6 met: the NeuroStore record reports only a between-group interaction contrast (patients with ADHD negative view > healthy controls neutral view) and no within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > view) or within-group task effects are provided. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli—IAPS images), I8 (clinical sample with control group reported separately), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise analysis with MNI peaks), I11 (whole-brain results reported in table). Inclusion criterion not met: I9 (no within-task contrast related to emotion regulation reported). Full text was available in the NeuroStore extraction. Based on the provided document, exclude under E6.

The record reports a task-based fMRI experiment using instructed emotion regulation (Decrease = reappraisal) versus look conditions, satisfying the review objective. Stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (aversive and neutral). Multiple within-task contrasts related to regulation are reported (e.g., Decrease > Look-Negative, Decrease > Look-Neutral) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are explicitly reported with peak coordinates in MNI and FWE correction. Sample (n=29 healthy) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and regulation was explicitly instructed). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be included.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal (MAINTAIN/INCREASE/DECREASE). Visual stimuli were static IAPS pictures (72 negative, 24 neutral). The sample includes borderline patients and healthy controls with results reported separately. The paper reports regulation-related contrasts (Decrease > Maintain, Increase > Maintain) and unregulated viewing contrasts (Negative > Neutral). Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with FWE-corrected results and tables of peak coordinates (e.g., Analyses 3,5,6 reporting whole-brain FWE-corrected maps and tables). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria apply (there are whole-brain results, not only ROI or connectivity). Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore record. Inclusion criteria applied: [I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11]. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

The study uses participant-generated autobiographical social anxiety situations and negative self-beliefs (NSBs) as stimuli and asks participants to reappraise these beliefs. These are non-visual, memory/script-driven or text-based self-referential stimuli rather than visual images or video; therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be visual). All other inclusion criteria are met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation / cognitive reappraisal), I8 (sample includes patients and healthy controls reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with standard-space coordinates), and I11 (results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Thus exclude for not meeting I7 (non-visual stimuli).

The NeuroStore record reports a task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual IAPS pictures with within-subject regulation contrasts (e.g. Reappraise > Attend). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation - reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported). However, all explicitly described statistical results in the record are reported with spatial scope = region of interest and FWE correction within ROIs; no analysis is clearly described as a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map with peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore the study appears to report ROI-only results and lacks the required whole-brain evidence (I10 not met). Exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI or SVC results with no whole-brain analysis) applies. Full text appears accessible in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study directly examines instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal/distancing) using visual IAPS stimuli in a task-based, event-related design with healthy participants (ages 10.5–22.9). The NeuroStore record reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation versus reactivity (e.g., Regulation/negative > Reactivity/negative) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise inference (AlphaSim corrected, cluster-level) with reported peak coordinates in MNI space (Analyses 3 and 4 report bold response peaks). Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). Although the paper also reports seed-based PPI connectivity analyses, it does not meet exclusion E5 because whole-brain task activation results are reported. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal up- and down-regulation, and distraction) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS and internet pictures). The sample (healthy adults) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., down-regulation > look aversive; up-regulation > look aversive; look aversive > look neutral) and includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (analyses 2 and 3 report FWE-corrected whole-brain results), with coordinates in MNI space. Although some results are ROI/SVC, whole-brain task activation maps are reported, so exclusion E4 does not apply. No exclusion criteria are met. All relevant inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied.

All inclusion criteria are satisfied: this is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs emotion regulation (reappraise, change image) consistent with cognitive reappraisal/antecedent-focused strategies (I6); stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7); participant groups include patients and healthy controls with group comparisons reported (I8); the paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (reappraise>maintain, maintain>just look, change image>maintain) (I9); multiple analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with permutation FWE TFCE correction and reported peaks/tables (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is empirical with original task activation maps, not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical, and it involves instructed regulation rather than mere perspective-taking. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the paper reports only region-of-interest–corrected task activation results and presents only between-group interaction contrasts, without a group-level whole-brain task activation map. Exclusion IDs met: E4 (ONLY ROI or SVC results / no whole-brain analysis) and E6 (ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions, with no within-group task effect reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map with peak coordinates in standard space). I11 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures) is not satisfied because I10 is not met. fulltext_incomplete=false

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: participants were instructed to 'watch the presented pictures' and there was no instructed emotion-regulation strategy (e.g. reappraisal, distancing). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS pictures), I8 (sample includes clinical group and controls), I9 (within-task valence factor / unregulated viewing contrasts present in the design), and I10 (group-level voxelwise results reported with MNI coordinates). The study is excluded because the regulated stimuli are idiographic autobiographical scripts and participant-generated negative self-belief statements (text/script-driven imagery), not visual stimuli, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli). It does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: reappraisal and acceptance), I9 (reports within-task regulation and viewing contrasts such as Reappraisal > React, Acceptance > React, React > Neutral), and I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore exclusion is solely due to failure to satisfy I7 (stimuli must be visual).

Excluded because the article reports only region-of-interest (ROI) results with no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps, thus meeting exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria not met: I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results reported; all analyses are ROI-based). Full text appears complete for screening.

This study must be excluded because all reported fMRI results are region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with small-volume correction and no whole-brain, voxelwise group maps are reported (violates I10 and meets exclusion E4). The study investigates instructed cognitive reappraisal of visual (negative/neutral) pictures with task-based fMRI and reports whole-brain interaction contrasts, but the NeuroStore record does not report any within-task (simple) regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > view) or within-group task activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation/reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample; patients with controls reported), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I9 (no clear within-task contrast related to emotion regulation is reported). No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met from the record. The study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using instructed emotion regulation (reappraise, suppress) (I6) with visual IAPS stimuli (I7). Samples include patients, siblings, and healthy controls with within-group results reported (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > attend; attend > suppress) (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise with peak coordinates in MNI space and cluster reporting (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: results include within-group whole-brain task activation maps (so not E4/E5/E6), the paper is empirical (not E3), and the task is regulation rather than mere perspective-taking (not E7). Reporting is sufficient for inclusion.

The study is an event-related task-based fMRI experiment that instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and in-house pictures). It reports within-subject, within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., REAPPRAISE > VIEW, VIEW > REAPPRAISE) and unregulated viewing contrasts. Multiple analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with cluster-corrected inference and reported peak coordinates in MNI (Tables t1/t2), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical, includes whole-brain activation maps (not ROI-only), and reports within-group task effects rather than only connectivity or between-group contrasts. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The NeuroStore record shows a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study with visual film stimuli (I5, I7) and an eligible sample (I8). Whole-brain peak coordinates are reported (I10) and results appear in tables/figures (I11). The reported contrast involves emotion-evoking versus neutral stimuli (EE > EN), satisfying the requirement for an emotion-related or unregulated viewing contrast (I9). However, the document provides no evidence that participants were instructed to apply an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal/distancing/acceptance instructions), so I6 is not met. Crucially, the extracted analyses are only between-group interaction contrasts (YP > RA and RA > YP for EE>EN) with no within-group task effects reported; thus the study reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions and meets exclusion criterion E6. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met). It does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli—faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrast: emotion > shape), I10 (whole-brain group-level analyses with peak coordinates), and I11 (results reported as tables of peaks). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no E3–E7 apply). Therefore exclusion is due to missing I6 (no instructed regulation).

This fMRI study directly tests instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal) versus look conditions using a visual-emotion task (IAPS and other images) in a healthy adolescent/young adult sample (n=78, ages 15–25). It reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Look Neg; Look Neg > Reappraise) with peak coordinates (Table) and whole-brain spatial scope noted for connectivity analyses, satisfying the requirement for group-level, voxelwise task-evoked maps. The study explicitly instructs reappraisal (reduce negative affect), uses visual stimuli, and includes appropriate within-group contrasts. Although some reported connectivity results use small-volume correction, whole-brain activation contrasts with reported peaks are present, so the study is not limited to ROI or connectivity-only results. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (Reappraise) consistent with cognitive reappraisal (I6). The regulated stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). The sample (clinical patients with SAD) is acceptable (I8). The report includes a within-task regulation contrast (Reappraise > Look Negative) and regression of symptom change (I9). At least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with reported peak coordinates in MNI space is provided (I10), and results are clearly described (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: results are whole-brain, not only ROI or connectivity, include within-group effects, and are not an empathy/perspective-taking-only paradigm. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

The study meets the review task and methods criteria (task-based fMRI; instructed cognitive reappraisal of visual IAPS images; healthy sample; reports within-task reappraisal contrasts). However, all reported results are region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (inference: "corrected within roi") and no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map or whole-brain peak coordinates are reported. Because only ROI / small-volume-corrected results are provided with no accompanying whole-brain analysis, exclusion criterion E4 applies and the study must be excluded for failing to meet I10 (whole-brain evidence). Specifics: contrasts reported include reappraise negative > watch negative (treatment interaction) and gPPI connectivity using an L amygdala seed, but these are ROI-limited.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task (I6) with visual stimuli (I7: IAPS/EmoPicS pictures and stories). The sample is children (I8) and the reported analyses include within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. negative-decrease; negative-attend; neutral-attend) (I9). At least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis is reported with peak coordinates in MNI space and cluster extent thresholding (I10), and results are presented as coordinates/tables (I11). No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are reported (so not E4), within-group effects are present (not E6), and the task clearly instructs regulation rather than mere perspective-taking (not E7).

Excluded because the study does not report any within-task contrast directly indexing emotion regulation (e.g., reappraise > attend/maintain) nor an unregulated visual viewing contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (regulation instruction—cognitive reappraisal), I8 (acceptable sample: healthy participants), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise results with coordinates in MNI), I11 (results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no within-task contrast related to emotion regulation or unregulated viewing contrast), I7 (unclear/absent visual emotional stimuli—the task uses opponent feedback and auditory white-noise punishments; emotional provocation appears not to be a standard visual stimulus). No exclusion criteria were directly violated (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Because the meta-analysis requires a within-task regulation contrast or visual-emotion viewing contrast, this study is excluded.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation that explicitly instructs emotion-regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) during both cue/anticipation and stimulus periods, using visual stimuli (63 negative IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g. Target Suppression > Target Appraise, Target Reappraisal > Target Appraise) at the group level, whole-brain, voxelwise, with FWE-corrected results and peak coordinates in MNI space. Participants (n=42 healthy adults) are described and standard screening was applied. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and include within-group effects). Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study uses task-based fMRI with instructed emotion regulation of visual IAPS stimuli, includes patient and control groups reported separately, and reports whole-brain, cluster-corrected task-evoked peaks in MNI coordinates. However, NeuroStore's extraction shows only omnibus between-group contrasts and interactions (BD vs SZ vs HC, BD vs HC, SZ vs HC, Group×Time interactions) and does not report any within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > view) or unregulated viewing contrasts. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I9 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Full text appears readable in the record.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: an emotion regulation strategy was not instructed. The paper examines dispositional (trait) reappraisal and reports correlations between trait reappraisal and anticipatory insula activity, explicitly stating there was no instruction to reappraise. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli—aversive and neutral images), I8 (eligible sample—healthy participants), I9 (reports within-task unregulated contrast: aversive > neutral anticipation), I10 (reports a whole-brain group-level analysis with peak coordinates), and I11 (results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Because I6 is not satisfied (no instructed regulation/manipulation), the study does not fit the meta-analysis requirement for instructed emotion regulation and must be excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: I5 task-based fMRI (event-related Emotion Regulation Task with BOLD measures), I6 instructed emotion regulation (explicit instructions to view/attend/reappraise/suppress), I7 visual stimuli (IAPS pictures), I8 sample qualifies (clinical patient group reported with participant details), I9 reports within-task contrast of interest (suppression > attend negative), I10 whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI reported, and I11 results are presented in tables. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), activation contrasts are reported (not only connectivity), and within-group effects are present. Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: there is no instruction to participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy during the fMRI task. Participants were instructed to expect and perceive IAPS pictures; groups reflect habitual (trait) suppression/reappraisal scores rather than instructed regulation during the task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli — IAPS), I8 (sample: healthy participants), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to emotional processing, e.g. negative expectation > neutral), I10 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with coordinates), I11 (results reported in tables). Exclusion criteria met: none. Because all required inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 is not met (no instructed regulation), the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

The NeuroStore record shows a task-based fMRI emotion regulation study using visual IAPS pictures with explicit auditory instructions to maintain, enhance, or diminish emotion (meets I5, I6, I7). Participants include patients and healthy controls reported separately; results are whole-brain, voxelwise, MNI-coordinate maps with cluster-correction (meets I8, I10, I11). However, the extracted analyses in this document list only between-group contrasts (patients > controls or controls > patients) and do not report any within-task contrasts such as reappraise/decline > maintain or similar for either group. Therefore the study fails I9 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts with no within-group task effect). Decision: EXCLUDED.

All inclusion criteria are met: task-based fMRI with instructed cognitive reappraisal (I5, I6) using visual IAPS images (I7). Both PTSD patients and healthy controls are reported with separate within-group Reappraise>Maintain contrasts (I8, I9). Multiple group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with MNI coordinates and cluster correction (AFNI 3dClustSim), and peaks/tables are provided (I10, I11). Although some ROI/SVC and connectivity results are present, whole-brain activation maps are also reported, so no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal (participants instructed to maintain, increase, or decrease responses) while viewing visual IAPS images. It reports appropriate within-task contrasts relevant to the review (e.g. negative > neutral; decrease > maintain; increase > maintain) and provides group-level whole-brain, voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (FWE-corrected whole-brain analyses reported). Sample comprises healthy adult participants. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical, reports whole-brain activation maps (not only ROI/SVC), includes within-group task effects, and is not an empathy-only perspective-taking study. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study with visual IAPS stimuli and a clinical sample (BPD with HC), and reports voxelwise whole-brain coordinates; however, the NeuroStore record contains no indication that participants were instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraise, distance, accept) and the reported analyses are between-group contrasts (BPD > HC or HC > BPD) for stimulus conditions. No within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) or within-group task effects are reported in the document. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I9 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports only between-group contrasts with no within-group task effect).

This study reports a task-based fMRI emotion regulation experiment using visual IAPS images with explicit instructions to decrease negative emotion via reappraisal (CHANGE vs LOOK). It includes patient (history of deliberate self-harm) and control groups with results reported separately. The analysis reports regulation-related contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results (Talairach coordinates, p<0.005 cluster-corrected, peaks in Table), satisfying meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and include within-task regulation contrasts rather than only between-group effects. Full text appears available in the extracted record.

Exclusion met: E5 (the paper reports only seed-based connectivity/PPI analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive reappraisal emotion regulation task), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS images), I8 (sample reporting: healthy participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no within-task activation contrast related to regulation reported as an activation map — only a connectivity contrast is reported), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates in standard space; the reported whole-brain result is a connectivity/PPI map rather than an activation contrast). The NeuroStore record lists only a voxelwise PPI connectivity analysis (amygdala seed) predicting connectivity during suppress>maintain; no task-evoked whole-brain activation contrasts are provided. Therefore the study must be excluded under E5.

EXCLUSION (E4): The paper reports only region-of-interest (ROI) results with inference corrected within the ROI and voxel-level FWE correction within the ROI; no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps or peak coordinates from whole-brain analyses are reported. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli: standardized facial photographs), I8 (clinical sample with separate groups reported), I9 (within-task contrasts reported, e.g. angry > fixation). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (the task is affect-labeling via button press, which is not clearly an instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal/acceptance per I6), I10 (no whole-brain evidence reported). Because E4 is met (ONLY ROI results reported), the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The study addresses the review objective and reports task-based fMRI of instructed cognitive reappraisal to visual stimuli in healthy children, with within-task contrasts (reappraise > view sad; view sad > neutral) and group-level whole-brain analyses. However, the NeuroStore record lists the coordinate space as 'OTHER' and does not provide peak coordinates in a standard anatomical space (e.g., MNI or Talairach) in the extracted fields. Inclusion criterion I10 requires whole-brain peak coordinates reported in a standard anatomical space; this criterion is not satisfied based on the document. Therefore the study must be excluded. Confidence is high because the record explicitly states the coordinate space.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using instructed emotion regulation (self-focused reappraisal to increase/decrease; I6) with visual stimuli (static angry and neutral faces; I7). The sample includes patients (MDD) and healthy controls reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Increase>Decrease, Decrease>Increase, within-group contrasts for HC and MDD) and unregulated viewing contrasts (view-angry>view-neutral; I9). Several analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with reported peak coordinates in MNI space (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain results are present (not ROI-only), it is empirical fMRI data, and not limited to connectivity or empathy-only instructions. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.
